candidates.exact_span: bacteria in the sewage sludge be less than three Most Probable Number per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed; at the time the sewage sludge is prepared for sale or given away in a bag or other container for application to the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a numeric pathogen limit and ties it to specific operational timing events; different readings of the limit value, dry-weight basis, or which timing event governs could change which enforceable limit applies and when monitoring/compliance must be demonstrated.

candidates.exact_span: Alternatives 5 and 6 are not authorized to demonstrate compliance with Class A sewage sludge in Texas permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Excludes two Class A compliance pathways in Texas; whether a facility relied on Alternatives 5 or 6 affects which numeric limits and monitoring demonstrations are legally available, and whether absent evidence for those alternatives is non-applicable or unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: The temperature of the sewage sludge that is used or disposed shall be maintained at a specific value for a period of time.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Alternative 1 compliance depends on unspecified temperature and duration values referenced elsewhere; interpretation of which values apply and whether they were maintained changes limit applicability and required monitoring.

candidates.exact_span: This alternative is not applicable to composting.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a facility's process qualifies as composting determines whether Alternative 1 monitoring and compliance obligations apply at all, affecting required-evidence versus not-required determinations.

candidates.exact_span: The pH of the sewage sludge that is used or disposed shall be raised to above 12 and shall remain above 12 for 72 hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes enforceable numeric pH and duration thresholds; different interpretations of measurement timing or the 72-hour continuity requirement could change compliance comparisons and monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: The pH shall be defined as the logarithm of the reciprocal of the hydrogen ion concentration measured at 25 degrees Celsius or measured at another temperature and then converted to an equivalent value at 25 degrees Celsius.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines how pH is measured and temperature-corrected; different interpretations of measurement temperature or conversion method could change whether the >12 threshold is met.

candidates.exact_span: The temperature of the sewage sludge shall be above 52 degrees Celsius for 12 hours or longer during the period that the pH of the sewage sludge is above 12.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Adds concurrent temperature and duration requirements tied to the elevated-pH period; interpretation of overlap between pH and temperature windows affects both limit exceedance findings and monitoring requirements.

candidates.exact_span: At the end of the 72 hour period during which the pH of the sewage sludge is above 12, the sewage sludge shall be air dried to achieve a percent solids in the sewage sludge greater than 50%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Imposes a post-treatment percent-solids numeric limit; different readings of when the 72-hour period ends or how percent solids is determined could change compliance results and required evidence.

candidates.exact_span: The sewage sludge shall be analyzed for enteric viruses prior to pathogen treatment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Mandates pre-treatment analysis; whether pathogen treatment has occurred and whether analysis predated it affects whether monitoring was required and how missing pre-treatment data is classified.

candidates.exact_span: The limit for enteric viruses is one Plaque-forming Unit per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) either before or following pathogen treatment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a numeric virus limit with permissive timing ('either before or following'); interpretation of which sampling point governs could change limit comparisons, monitoring applicability, and whether absent data is for a required or optional period.

candidates.exact_span: The sewage sludge shall be analyzed for viable helminth ova prior to pathogen treatment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Requires pre-treatment helminth ova analysis; interpretation of treatment timing determines whether this monitoring obligation was triggered and how missing results are categorized.

candidates.exact_span: The limit for viable helminth ova is less than one per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) either before or following pathogen treatment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets a numeric helminth ova limit with ambiguous sampling timing; different readings of 'before or following' affect which measurement is compared to the limit and whether missing data reflects a required monitoring window.

candidates.exact_span: The density of enteric viruses in the sewage sludge shall be less than one Plaque- forming Unit per four grams of total solids (dry weight bas is) at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed or at the time the sludge is prepared for sale or give away in a bag or other container for application to the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Alternative 4 sets a virus density limit tied to use/disposal or container-preparation events; interpretation of which event applies and the stated units/threshold could change limit applicability and required sampling timing.

candidates.exact_span: The density of viable helminth ova in the sewage sludge shall be less than one per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed or at the time the sewage sludge is prepared for sale or give away in a bag or other container for application to the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Alternative 4 sets a helminth ova density limit with multiple triggering events; different readings of which operational moment governs could change compliance comparisons and monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be treated by one of the Processes to Further Reduce Pathogens (PFRP) described in 503 Appendix B.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Alternative 5 substitutes process-based pathogen reduction for direct numeric sampling; whether a process qualifies as an authorized PFRP changes which limits apply and what monitoring evidence is required.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be treated by a process that is equivalent to a Process to Further Reduce Pathogens, if individually approved by the Pathogen Equivalency Committee representing the EPA.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Alternative 6 compliance hinges on equivalency and individual EPA committee approval; interpretation of whether approval exists affects available compliance pathways and whether missing approval evidence is unresolved or non-applicable.

candidates.exact_span: Four alternatives are available to demonstrate compliance with Class B sewage sludge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Frames the set of permissible Class B demonstration pathways; misidentifying which alternatives are in play affects which monitoring requirements apply and how absent pathway-specific evidence is interpreted.

candidates.exact_span: Alternatives 2, 3, and 4 are not authorized to demonstrate compliance with Class B sewage sludge in Texas permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Removes three Class B compliance pathways in Texas; whether a facility attempted to use Alternatives 2–4 changes which limits and monitoring demonstrations are enforceable and how missing data for those alternatives is classified.
